We are seeking a strategic and solutions-oriented Director, Creative Operations to lead the operational backbone of our in-house creative team. As a key leader within the organization, you will be responsible for driving efficiency, optimizing workflows, and enabling the seamless delivery of creative work for a global audience.

This role will lead project management, creative operations systems, technology enablement, and external agency partnerships to ensure our teams deliver best-in-class creative work at scale. You will collaborate closely with Digital & Technology, Brand, Marketing, and Production teams to shape and evolve the creative operating model, lead technology initiatives, and identify opportunities to improve speed, quality, and efficiency through automation and emerging technologies.

The ideal candidate is a highly organized and collaborative leader with deep expertise in creative operations, workflow transformation, technology implementation, and change management. You are equally comfortable developing long-term operational strategies and ensuring day-to-day execution excellence.

Creative Operations & Project Management

• 
Lead the Creative Studio operating model, including intake, prioritization, capacity planning, resource allocation, and project delivery.

• 
Drive continuous improvement of creative workflows, systems, and governance across project management, DAM, and MRM platforms.

• 
Partner with Creative, Brand, Marketing Operations, Production, and Technology teams to align priorities, optimize resources, and ensure successful delivery.

• 
Establish operational KPIs and reporting to measure workflow effectiveness, resource utilization, delivery performance, and business impact.

• 
Lead and develop Creative Operations capabilities through coaching, best practices, and process excellence.

Technology, AI & Operational Excellence

• 
Partner with Digital & Technology teams to evaluate, select, and implement creative technology solutions, including DAM, workflow, automation, and AI-enabled tools.

• 
Develop business cases and investment plans that improve creative effectiveness, operational efficiency, and scalability.

• 
Establish governance, adoption frameworks, and responsible-use practices for AI and emerging technologies.

• 
Monitor industry trends and translate innovation into practical improvements across creative operations and content production.

Agency & Vendor Management

• 
Lead relationships with external design, localization, customization, and technology partners, ensuring alignment with brand, quality, budget, and delivery expectations.

• 
Manage SOWs, contracts, performance metrics, and ongoing vendor effectiveness.

• 
Evaluate partner capabilities and identify opportunities to leverage innovation, automation, and emerging production models.

Change Management & Transformation

• 
Lead change initiatives that enable successful adoption of new technologies, processes, and ways of working.

• 
Drive continuous improvement and build organizational capability in creative operations, technology adoption, and operational excellence.

• 
Influence stakeholders across the business to deliver sustainable transformation and measurable impact.

Budget & Resource Management

• 
Own budget planning for Creative Operations systems, technology investments, and operational needs in partnership with the Head of Production.

• 
Forecast and optimize resource allocation across internal teams and external partners.

• 
Partner with Finance and Production to monitor spend, measure ROI, and drive efficiency across people, processes, and technology.

Qualifications & Experience

• 
Significant experience in Creative Operations, Project Management, Marketing Operations, or workflow transformation within an in-house agency, creative organization, or related environment.

• 
Experience leading or shaping creative operations functions, operating models, or large-scale transformation initiatives.

• 
Expertise in enterprise project management, DAM, MRM, workflow management, and collaboration platforms (e.g., Workfront, Asana, Wrike, Bynder, Aprimo, or similar).

• 
Experience evaluating, implementing, and scaling AI-enabled or automation solutions within creative, marketing, or operational environments.

• 
Experience leading RFPs, developing business cases, and delivering technology implementations in partnership with Digital & Technology teams.

• 
Strong understanding of creative workflows across design, content production, localization, and asset management.

• 
Demonstrated success managing agency and vendor partnerships, including localization, customization, and technology providers.

• 
Strong stakeholder management, communication, and change leadership skills.

• 
Proven ability to drive adoption of new technologies and ways of working across complex organizations.

• 
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities.

• 
Experience with budget planning, financial management, and investment prioritization.

• 
Passion for leveraging technology, automation, and innovation to improve creative effectiveness and operational excellence.

Reports to: VP Brand Creative

Why Join Us?

This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of Creative Operations at Pandora. You will play a critical role in building the processes, systems, and capabilities that enable exceptional creative work at a global scale. Working across Brand Creative, Production, Marketing, and Technology, you will help define how creativity is delivered in a modern, technology-enabled organization while driving meaningful impact across the business.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced and driven Program Manager to lead the establishment of HR Shared Services Center (SSC), a key pillar in our HR transformation journey, driving the design, planning, and implementation of this strategic initiative.

In this role, you will establish a program organization and lead multiple workstreams and coordinate timelines, resources, budgets, stakeholders and risks to ensure the successful implementation of our HR Shared Services Center. You know which priorities to recommend, what to communicate to the HR organization and when to involve other corporate functions if necessary. Furthermore, you will bring together people, processes, technology and organisational change to establish an efficient, scalable and high-quality HR service delivery model.

Welcome to Global HR

You will join Demant's Global HR organization and work closely with HR Core Deliveries, business units, Shared Services C operations teams and stakeholders across the global organization.

Our approximately 400 HR professionals work globally to attract, develop and empower the people who drive Demant's continued success. As a global leader in hearing healthcare and hearing aid technology, Demant is on an ambitious transformation journey. In this role, you will help shape how HR services are delivered and experienced across the organization.

Lead the HR Shared Services Center Transition

As Program Manager for HR SSC, you will manage the day-to-day implementation of the SSC transition, coordinating multiple workstreams and ensuring alignment throughout the implementation. Working closely with senior leadership, HR Core Deliveries, business units, SSC operations and project leads, you will maintain momentum, manage risks and dependencies, and ensure clear communication and decision-making. You will also help ensure business continuity and successful adoption of the new HR service delivery model.

In this role, you will:

• 
Lead program delivery, including plans, milestones, budgets, KPIs, governance and coordination of multiple workstreams.

• 
Be responsible for the business case

• 
Track project progress against established milestones, KPIs and business case

• 
Drive stakeholder alignment and communication, facilitating collaboration across senior leadership, HR, business units and SSC operations.

• 
Manage resources, risks and dependencies, ensuring appropriate allocation of capacity and timely escalation and resolution of issues.

• 
Oversee transition and change activities, supporting adoption and maintaining business continuity throughout implementation.

• 
Ensure effective reporting and project governance, including dashboards, steering committee materials, decisions, actions and lessons learned.

• 
Ensure quality and compliance, including appropriate acceptance criteria and consideration of country-specific legal and regulatory requirements.

What You Bring

You hold a bachelor's or master’s degree in business administration, Human Resources, Project Management, Organizational Development or a related field.

You have significant project management/program management experience, including large-scale transformation or Shared Services Center establishment and transition initiatives. You have successfully managed complex, multi-workstream projects involving substantial budgets and diverse stakeholders, preferably within HR operations or HR transformation.

You have great knowledge of project management methodologies and tools. PMP certification or equivalent is an advantage, as is experience with platforms such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Asana or similar.

Experience with HR systems and processes is important, with knowledge of SAP SuccessFactors, ServiceNow or similar solutions considered an advantage. You are also highly proficient in Microsoft Office and comfortable working with project dashboards, reporting and data. As a colleague, you are structured, collaborative and solution oriented. You create clarity and momentum in complex environments and can lead cross-functional teams without direct authority. You communicate assertively with both project teams and senior executives and are comfortable working across cultures and geographies.

Furthermore, you are analytical and pragmatic, with good problem-solving and stakeholder management skills. You combine project management discipline with business acumen and an understanding of HR operations and organisational dynamics.

Finally, you have a good compliance mindset and understand the importance of balancing country-specific requirements with global standards and objectives.

Come and join us

This is an opportunity to take a central role in a significant HR transformation and help shape the future delivery of HR services across Demant.

You will work with experienced colleagues and senior stakeholders across the global organization and have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on how HR services are delivered, scaled and continuously improved.

If you enjoy complex transformations, international collaboration and turning ambitious plans into successful execution, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Test Method Specialist, Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory
jobs.description:
Imagine if robust test methods and reliable test equipment helped ensure the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products. That is where you come in.

As our new Test Method Specialist, you will become the technical focal point for selected test methods and related equipment in Coloplast Mørdrup, primarily supporting the QA Lifecycle Laboratory and Pilot SVS. This is a practical, hands-on specialist role in which you will work directly with laboratory equipment, including troubleshooting, service and calibration follow-up, qualification, and software and computer upgrades. You will support the full test method and equipment lifecycle, from implementation and qualification to maintenance, transfer and continuous improvement.

If you are motivated by hands-on technical problem-solving, equipment responsibility, quality assurance and data evaluation, this role offers meaningful responsibility and broad organisational impact. You will also work closely with many internal and external stakeholders, making clear communication, coordination and strong stakeholder management an important part of your success.

“In this role, your technical judgement and ability to create robust solutions will help ensure reliable test results and compliant laboratory processes throughout the product lifecycle,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of laboratory technicians and test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations and test method activities.

You will be part of an engaged team with a strong mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, Operations, Global Test Method teams and international manufacturing sites. We value curiosity, knowledge sharing, flexibility and a continuous improvement mindset.

Own and develop test methods and equipment

As Test Method Specialist, you will act as a one-point contact and technical superuser for selected test methods and test equipment. A significant part of the role is practical equipment responsibility. You will work hands-on with equipment and coordinate activities to ensure it is qualified, calibrated, serviced, maintained and performing as intended. You will also support software and computer upgrades connected to the equipment, as well as reliable data handling and traceability.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

•    Acting as technical owner and one-point contact for selected test methods and related test equipment

•    Planning, coordinating and performing qualification of test equipment, including relocation, capacity expansion and replacement of critical parts

•    Preparing and maintaining qualification protocols, reports, procedures, test method documentation and one-point lessons when needed

•    Performing hands-on troubleshooting of test equipment and methods, evaluating test results and leading root cause investigations when failures occur

•    Taking practical responsibility for test equipment, including service activities, calibration follow-up, preventive maintenance and ensuring that equipment performs as intended

•    Handling changes, nonconformities and CAPAs related to test methods, calibration and test equipment

•    Supporting compliant storage and traceability of raw data before product release

•    Planning and participating in transfers of test methods and equipment to international manufacturing sites

•    Providing technical support and sparring to colleagues in the Pilot Plant, Global Operations and international manufacturing sites

•    Collaborating with Global Test Method teams and contributing technical input to the development and improvement of test methods

•    Training specialists, laboratory technicians, operators and other users in test methods, test principles and use of equipment

•    Coordinating software and computer upgrades for test equipment, assessing their impact on qualification and documentation, and managing suppliers, service visits and relevant service agreements

•    Participating in internal and external audits related to test methods, equipment and documentation

•    Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, systems and ways of working

Bring strong technical judgement and a quality mindset

To succeed in this position, you combine technical depth with a structured, practical and hands-on approach. You enjoy working directly with equipment, take ownership and work systematically when resolving technical issues. You are comfortable making decisions based on data, risk and regulatory requirements.

The role involves close collaboration with many internal and external stakeholders, therefor you communicate clearly, coordinate effectively and are able to build strong working relationships across functions, sites and suppliers.

We imagine that you bring:

•   A master’s degree within science, engineering, mechanics, physics, chemistry, pharmacy or a comparable technical field, or have at least five years of relevant experience with test methods

•   Solid hands-on experience with test methods, measurement principles and qualification of laboratory or production test equipment

•   Strong problem-solving skills and experience with structured root cause analysis

•   Confident evaluating, analysing and presenting technical data skills, including the use of statistical methods

•   Ability to write, review and understand technical documentation, protocols and reports

•   Knowledge of quality systems and regulated environments; knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and GMP is an advantage

•   An understanding of validation, calibration, design control, specifications and process risk management

•   Abitlity to plan and prioritise your work effectively and follow activities through to completion

•   Strong stakeholder management skills and collaborate effectively across disciplines, functions, geographical locations and external suppliers

•    Communicating skills professionally in English, both written and spoken; Danish is an advantage

•    A comfortable competence using digital tools for documentation, data analysis and traceability; experience with Microsoft Office, Veeva, JMP or similar systems is an advantage

A specialist role with broad impact

This is a permanent specialist position in the QA Lifecycle Laboratory. The role has no direct reports and includes collaboration with international colleagues and manufacturing sites. Some travel may be expected in connection with transfers, supplier activities and site support.

You will join a working environment where quality, safety, technical excellence, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are central to our daily work. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network and influence how test methods and equipment are managed across the product lifecycle.

Interested?

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Financial Analyst, you'll own the day-to-day financial planning and analysis (FP&A) across clinical programmes, research and corporate functions. You'll turn financial data and input from colleagues into reliable forecasts, useful insights and clear reporting that helps Hemab make informed decisions.

Working closely with the FP&A Director, you'll take ownership of recurring financial activities while helping build practical ways of working as Hemab grows. Your work will give our teams greater financial clarity and help us make thoughtful decisions about the resources behind our science.

What you'll do

• Own monthly FP&A activities across assigned clinical studies, research projects and functions, keeping forecasts accurate and up to date.

• Partner with functional leads and project teams to understand spending, challenge assumptions and identify financial risks and opportunities early.

• Coordinate quarterly forecasts and contribute to the annual Investment Plan and Long-Range Plan.

• Analyse actuals against forecasts, explain variances and turn financial information into clear, useful insights.

• Prepare management reporting, financial commentary and decision materials for review by the FP&A Director.

• Maintain and improve Power BI reporting, ensuring reliable data and consistent financial information.

• Manage routine financial follow-up with CROs and vendors, including invoice reviews, change orders and financial input to negotiations.

• Build straightforward financial frameworks and reporting practices that help teams work efficiently as Hemab grows.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience in FP&A, forecasting, management reporting and financial business partnering.

• Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to turn complex information into practical recommendations.

• Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with Power BI.

• Experience managing forecasts independently, identifying material changes and knowing when to escalate.

• Ability to work effectively with finance and non-finance colleagues, communicate clearly and challenge assumptions constructively.

• Professional fluency in English.

Nice to have

• Experience in biotech, pharma, clinical development, CROs or another project-driven environment.

• Familiarity with clinical study budgets, vendor financial management or financial planning systems.

• Experience improving financial reporting or building ways of working in a growing organisation.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

We value people who take ownership, solve problems, ask for help when needed and work without ego. At our size, how you work matters as much as your CV. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the numbers, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Purpose of the role

Your purpose is to help keep our crisis-management setup current, organised and ready for use. You will support documents, exercises, readiness activities, reporting and follow-up, while learning how operational resilience and executive crisis management work in a large infrastructure company.

Key responsibilities

• Maintain and improve crisis plans, appendices, role descriptions, quick guides, checklists and templates.
